title: Creation in the Brahma Purana: How the World Began Again
desc: The Brahma Purana's story of creation after the great dissolution: Vasudeva, Brahma on the lotus, the five elements and the four kinds of life.
alt: Vishnu resting on the cosmic waters with Brahma on the lotus, Brahma Purana creation story
caption: Vishnu on the cosmic waters: the starting point of creation in the Brahma Purana.
intro: The **Brahma Purana creation story** begins where everything else has ended: after a **great dissolution (pralaya)** that leaves only darkness. This post retells how, according to the Purana, **Vasudeva** wakes from yogic sleep and the world begins again.
takeaways: The Purana says the world is **made again and again**, not once.
**Vasudeva** is the awake presence behind the darkness, holding the roles of creator, protector and dissolver.
**Brahma** appears on a lotus, then the **five elements** follow, then all living beings.
Living things are grouped into **four kinds by birth**: womb, egg, moisture and seed.

p: At the end of a cosmic age, the **Brahma Purana** says, a great dissolution swallows everything. Everything that moves and everything that stands still is gone. There is only darkness.

Behind that darkness one presence stays awake. The text calls him **Vasudeva**, the Supreme Being who holds the three roles of **creator, protector and dissolver**. When he rises from his yogic sleep, creation starts again.

From a **lotus that grows from his navel**, Brahma appears, glowing like the petals around him. Then come the **five elements**: air, water, fire, earth and space, first in a subtle form and then in a solid one. Everything that follows is built from them.

Through Brahma, the Supreme brings forth the sages beginning with **Marichi**, the gods, the ancestors (pitrus), the sacrifices, and groups such as vidyadharas and yakshas. Animals follow, from monkeys to lions.
The Purana sorts all living things by how they are born:
The creator then divides himself, the **right half as man and the left as woman**. From that pair, creation continues by generation.

Having made all this, Brahma goes into deep meditation and merges into the nature of Vasudeva. After a time he takes the Vasudeva form himself, and the Purana pictures a great being with a **thousand eyes, feet and heads**. The text then moves on to the sacred places of the earth.

It is one of the oldest patterns in Indian thought: the world is not made once. It is made again and again, and the same awareness lies beneath every cycle. For a reader today, the point is **humility**. We live inside one cycle of a very large process.

faq.q: What does the Brahma Purana say about creation?
faq.a: It says that after a great dissolution only darkness remained, until **Vasudeva** woke, created **Brahma** on a lotus, and the five elements and all beings followed.

faq.q: Who is Vasudeva in the Brahma Purana?
faq.a: Vasudeva is the Supreme Being who holds the roles of **creator, protector and dissolver**, and is the awareness behind every cycle of creation.

faq.q: What are the four kinds of living beings?
faq.a: The Purana groups them by birth: from the **womb, eggs, moisture and sweat, and seeds**.

note: This is a retelling in our own words, based on the Brahma Purana as presented in a Telugu prose edition.
